Programme Analyst - 2 Year Fixed-Term - Cambridgeshire County Council

We are looking for an analyst to join our Adult Social Care transformation programme. This post is a fixed-term appointment of 2 years, funded through a government grant.

About the programme
The programme will redesign how residents get support in later life. It involves new digital services, a refreshed approach to assessments and closer working with the NHS. Around 30 people work on it, from social workers to software developers.

The post
As programme analyst, you will gather evidence about current processes, model options and track the benefits. You will work alongside service managers and project managers and report to the programme lead.

You will:
- Analyse data on demand, cost and outcomes
- Map processes and find where delays happen
- Develop business cases for new ideas
- Create dashboards to track progress
- Write clear papers for the programme board
- Facilitate workshops with practitioners and residents

You will have:
- At least three years' experience as a business or data analyst
- Strong Excel and the ability to learn new tools
- Experience of writing business cases
- The ability to explain complex issues simply
- Interest in social care (experience is not needed)

We offer 25 days leave, the Local Government Pension Scheme, flexible and hybrid working, and a supportive manager. Salary is 40,000 to 44,000.

Secondees from other organisations are welcome to apply. The closing date is 30 November, with interviews in early December. Please complete the online form.

Application Support Analyst - Willowbank Retail Systems (Telford)

Willowbank is a software company providing till and stock management systems to independent shops. Our support team of fourteen is proud of its reputation for friendly, quick answers. Between them, the team has over 70 years of combined experience with our products, so there is always somebody who knows the answer.

The opportunity
We have a vacancy for an application support analyst to help customers get the best from our software. You will take calls and tickets, investigate problems, reproduce bugs and work with developers to fix them.

What you will do
- Diagnose issues using logs and SQL queries
- Guide customers through fixes by phone and screen share
- Raise defects with clear steps to reproduce
- Test new releases before they go out
- Write articles for our knowledge base
- Share information in daily team huddles

What you will bring
- 4-6 years in application or technical support, ideally for a software product
- SQL knowledge to a good level
- Strong written and spoken communication
- Patience with users who are having a bad day
- Retail experience would be useful, since our customers will talk to you about shelves, tills and stock

The deal
- Salary 32,000 to 38,000
- 24 days holiday plus bank holidays, rising by a day for each year of service up to 30
- Pension and health cash plan
- Hybrid working after probation
- Free parking and a cycle scheme

Apply with a CV, and tell us about a problem you solved that others had given up on. Interview is by video, followed by a visit to our offices.

IT Programme Director - Interim - Southampton

Introducing Calloway Interim Executives
Calloway Interim Executives has been placing senior interim managers for 30 years, from specialist directors through to complete turnaround teams. We act for FTSE 250 and public sector clients and are known for matching the right person to the right challenge.

The assignment
Our client is a port and logistics operator on the south coast. After an acquisition, it needs an experienced IT programme director to lead the integration of two technology estates.

You will report to the Group CIO and lead a team of six programme and project managers. You will take over the plan, test its assumptions, reset it where needed and deliver the integration over the next nine months.

Duties
- Set direction and governance for the integration
- Manage a budget of 12 million pounds
- Resolve conflicts between the two legacy teams
- Handle supplier negotiations and contract changes
- Report to the board and the finance director
- Keep staff morale high through change

Experience required
- A minimum of 8 years running large IT programmes, including at least one post-acquisition integration
- Excellent stakeholder leadership at board level
- Knowledge of ERP, port operating systems or similar
- Commercial awareness and negotiation skill
- Certification in MSP or equivalent is useful

Terms
Daily rate 900 to 1,100. Location: Southampton with some travel. Start: January.

To apply, send your CV to our interim team. All conversations are confidential, and we will not send your details to our client without your agreement.

IT Technician - Hallam Manufacturing (Sheffield)

Hallam Manufacturing makes components for the automotive industry and employs 450 people at a single site. Our IT team of five keeps the business running, from the machines on the shop floor to the laptops in the office.

Why we are advertising
One of our technicians has completed his 4 year apprenticeship with us and is moving to a systems role. We now need to replace him. We have a history of growing people internally, with many of our managers having started as apprentices.

The role
- Handle first and second line support for around 200 users
- Maintain PCs, printers and shop floor terminals
- Manage user accounts and permissions in Active Directory
- Support the network team during upgrades
- Run backups and check them
- Ensure assets are logged and equipment is ready for new starters
- Provide cover for the helpdesk during holidays

Requirements
- At least 2 years' experience in IT support, whether in an office or industrial environment
- Knowledge of Windows 10 and 11, Microsoft 365 and basic networking
- Practical, calm and clear with non-technical users
- Willing to work in a factory environment, including wearing safety boots and glasses
- Full UK driving licence preferred

What you get
Salary 28,000 to 32,000, 25 days holiday plus the Christmas shutdown, a pension, free lunch on Fridays and on-site parking. We also pay for professional qualifications and encourage staff to take them.

Apply with a CV and a covering note. Shortlisted candidates will be invited for a site tour and interview with the IT manager.

Database Administrator - Oracle and SQL Server - Hybrid, Cheltenham

Overview
A government-linked organisation requires a Database Administrator to join its infrastructure team. Our client looks after information on millions of citizens, so reliability and care are part of daily life.

The platform
You will be responsible for Oracle and SQL Server estates, supporting live services and development environments. Transaction logs are kept for 90 days. Archived records must be retained for 7 years under legal obligation, and you will help to maintain the processes that guarantee that.

Responsibilities
- Install, configure and upgrade database servers
- Monitor performance and tune queries
- Manage backups, restores and disaster recovery tests
- Apply patches and security updates
- Support developers with design and optimisation
- Maintain documentation and capacity plans
- Take part in an on-call rota, with additional payment

Skills and experience
- 6 years or more as a DBA with Oracle in a production environment
- SQL Server administration (desirable but expected to be learned on the job)
- Scripting in Bash or PowerShell
- Understanding of high availability, such as Data Guard or Always On
- Disciplined approach to change control

Package
Salary 58,000 to 66,000, 28 days holiday, civil service style pension, hybrid working with two days on site, and training allowance.

Security
Clearance (BPSS, then SC) is required. Applicants must be British citizens or have settled status. To apply, send a CV by email. The agency will arrange a call to discuss the role in more detail.

Senior Business Intelligence Developer - Hayward Group (Nottingham)

Hayward Group is an engineering and facilities business with 3,000 employees. Our data team has grown from two people to twelve, and we plan to double it.

About our team
We have a strong culture of progression. Most of our analysts become senior within 3 years, and several have become team leaders. We publish levels and expectations openly, so you can see exactly how to grow.

The role
As a senior BI developer, you will design the data models and reports that managers use daily, and mentor junior colleagues as they develop. You will work with finance, operations and HR to turn data into decisions.

Duties
- Build and maintain data models in Power BI
- Design data warehouse structures in Azure Synapse
- Write efficient SQL and DAX
- Establish standards for reports and naming
- Review colleagues' work and coach juniors
- Gather requirements and present prototypes to stakeholders
- Monitor usage and refine reports

Requirements
- 5 years of working in a BI development role
- Strong skills with Power BI, SQL and dimensional modelling
- Experience with Azure data services
- Good communication with senior stakeholders
- A bachelor's degree or equivalent

Benefits
Salary 52,000 to 62,000, annual bonus, 26 days holiday, pension, private healthcare, hybrid working with three days in our Nottingham office, and a learning budget of 1,500 each year.

Apply with a CV and a recent example of a dashboard or report you have built (anonymised, please). Interviews take place in two stages, with a technical task in the second.

Head of Software Engineering - Leighton Digital Studios

Leighton Digital Studios is an award-winning software house with 25 years of experience building bespoke systems for banks, insurers and government agencies. Founded by engineers, we are still led by engineers and we say no to work that does not interest us.

Position summary
We are appointing a Head of Software Engineering to manage our 45 developers, testers and architects across three offices. You will report to the Managing Director and be responsible for technical quality, delivery and people.

What you will do
- Lead, grow and retain a high-performing engineering team
- Set technical standards and ensure they are followed
- Manage resource allocation between client projects
- Support the sales team with technical input on proposals
- Resolve technical and delivery escalations with clients
- Introduce modern practices without disrupting live work
- Develop the team's careers through coaching and training

What we require
- At least 10 years in software engineering, with several in leadership roles
- Experience of managing teams of 30 or more
- Strong knowledge of .NET, cloud-native design and CI/CD
- Commercial awareness in a consultancy or professional services environment
- Excellent communication and the capacity to inspire

What you receive
Salary 95,000 to 115,000, bonus, 30 days holiday, private health and dental cover, pension, car allowance and the chance to join the leadership team.

Our offices are in Manchester, Leeds and Bristol. You will be expected to spend two days a week in the main office. Applications go through our recruitment partner; please email your CV and we will arrange an initial conversation.

Business Analyst (SC Clearance) - Home Office Programme - Hybrid, Croydon

Our client, a government supplier, is working on a large immigration technology programme and needs business analysts to join several delivery teams.

Programme background
The programme is rebuilding case management tools for caseworkers who make decisions on applications. It is a multi-supplier programme following agile delivery practices, and the teams are friendly and collaborative.

The role
You will work with caseworkers, product owners and developers to understand how work is done today and how to make it better. You will write user stories, map processes and support testing.

Responsibilities
- Run discovery sessions with caseworkers
- Document current and future processes
- Break epics into stories with acceptance criteria
- Refine the backlog with the product owner
- Support the team during sprint demonstrations
- Identify risks, dependencies and data needs

Skills and experience
- 3 years minimum as a business analyst, ideally in a government or agile environment
- Strong stakeholder skills and a calm approach
- Competence with Jira and Confluence
- Knowledge of GDS service standards is desirable

Security
SC clearance is mandatory. To be eligible, you need to have lived in the UK for the past 5 years without significant breaks. Candidates with existing clearance will be prioritised. Without it, we cannot proceed.

Rates are 450 to 520 per day, outside IR35. The initial term is until the end of the financial year, with likely extension. Interviews are conducted online.

Send your CV to apply, noting your clearance status and availability.

Infrastructure Architect - Ferrant Utilities Group (Hybrid, Glasgow)

At Ferrant Utilities we keep the lights on for 1.2 million homes. Our technology teams support control rooms, customer systems and field operations, and it is critical that they never stop.

Our culture
We look after people. After 5 years of service you receive an extra five days leave, and every 10 years brings a long-service award and a paid sabbatical month. Many colleagues have been with us a long time, and we are proud of it.

The role
We need an infrastructure architect to design the platforms on which our next generation of services will run. You will define how we use cloud, on-premise and edge technologies safely and efficiently.

Responsibilities
- Create target architectures and roadmaps for infrastructure
- Review designs from project teams and suppliers
- Set standards for hosting, networking and resilience
- Advise on risk and cost
- Represent infrastructure in design authority forums
- Partner with operational technology teams
- Mentor engineers

You will have
- 7 years or more in infrastructure engineering or architecture
- Expert knowledge of virtualisation, networking and storage
- Practical experience of Azure
- Understanding of critical national infrastructure security expectations
- TOGAF or similar architecture certification would be an advantage

Benefits
Salary 75,000 to 88,000, pension (defined benefit for existing members; defined contribution for new joiners), 30 days holiday, flexible hours, healthcare and a car allowance.

To apply, send your CV and a short summary of an architecture you designed and what you would change. We will respond to every candidate.

Release Manager - Banking Platform Programme - Edinburgh

THE PROGRAMME
Our client is a UK bank delivering a 3 year programme to move its mortgage business to a new platform. The programme is in its second quarter, with several delivery teams now live. It involves multiple suppliers, shared environments and lots of coordination.

THE ROLE
As release manager, you will plan and coordinate software releases across environments, from test to production. You will make sure that every release is safe, approved and communicated.

KEY TASKS
- Maintain the release calendar and manage conflicts
- Chair the weekly change and release meeting
- Coordinate environments and deployment activities with engineering teams
- Run go/no-go decisions with product owners and operations
- Handle post-release checks and incident reviews
- Improve release processes and automation
- Produce release reports for the programme board

REQUIREMENTS
- Four or more years of release management in a regulated environment
- Strong understanding of CI/CD and DevOps
- Knowledge of ITIL change and release practices
- Experience with ServiceNow or similar tools
- Excellent organisation and communication
- Calm in a crisis, and clear when it matters

TERMS
This role is available on a contract basis (inside IR35) for six months in the first instance, with expected extensions. Day rate: 500 to 580. Based in Edinburgh, with two days on site per week. Interviews: one stage.

To apply, send your CV with your availability. We will respond to suitable applicants within one working day.

Cloud Platform Lead - Fintech Scale-up - Remote UK

BACKGROUND
Bluefen Payments was founded 9 years ago to make payments simpler for small businesses. Today it processes billions of pounds for its merchants. The engineering team of fifty sits within the wider technology function of about a hundred.

THE OPPORTUNITY
You will lead the cloud platform team, which looks after the infrastructure, tooling and reliability of our services. We run on AWS, and the platform team provides the paved road that our developers travel.

RESPONSIBILITIES
- Lead a team of five platform engineers
- Own the roadmap for infrastructure, deployment and observability
- Keep cost, reliability and security in balance
- Respond to major incidents and lead the reviews afterwards
- Work with security and compliance on PCI DSS requirements
- Advise on architecture decisions across engineering
- Recruit and develop platform engineers

EXPERIENCE
- At least 5 years in infrastructure, DevOps or SRE roles, of which a minimum of 3 years in AWS
- Experience leading or mentoring engineers
- Strong knowledge of Terraform, Kubernetes and CI/CD
- Understanding of security in a regulated environment
- A practical approach to reliability, with monitoring and runbooks

BENEFITS
- Salary 85,000 to 100,000 plus share options
- 30 days holiday
- Pension with 7 percent employer contribution
- Home-office budget and co-working allowance
- Two company meetups each year

APPLYING
Send us your CV, along with a note about the most interesting reliability problem you have solved. We will invite you to a conversation with our CTO, followed by a technical discussion with two engineers.
note: firm requirement is highest lower bound (5, not 3)
